t: Mentuhotep II of Thebes reunited Egypt, and the Twelfth Dynasty ruled it from a new residence, Itjtawy, near el-Lisht.
Kings built a bureaucratic state, curbed provincial governors, reclaimed the Faiyum and fortified the Nubian frontier at Semna.
Its literature and Middle Egyptian language became classics, studied by Egyptian scribes for some two thousand years.
dyk: The Rhind Mathematical Papyrus, one of the main sources for Egyptian mathematics, was copied under the Hyksos from an original written in the reign of Amenemhat III.
ev: Mentuhotep II becomes king at Thebes and later reunites Egypt
Amenemhat I founds the Twelfth Dynasty and the residence of Itjtawy
Senusret I takes sole power and conquers Lower Nubia to the Second Cataract
Senusret III sets up a boundary stele at Semna fixing the Nubian frontier
Amenemhat III begins a long reign of Faiyum reclamation and pyramid building
Sobekneferu, last ruler of the Twelfth Dynasty, ends her reign
The Hyksos take Memphis and Itjtawy is abandoned
